posts.text: Astera Labs is the cleanest way to own the sentence 'the bottleneck moved from the chip to the wire'. Rack-scale accelerator deployments turn the fabric between GPUs into the scarce resource, and retimers, gearboxes and the telemetry stack around them are content that scales with rack count rather than with unit shipments. Why now: PCIe 6.0 silicon is reaching production volume across the ecosystem and the scale-up interconnect question is being settled in standards committees this year rather than in benchmarks. The desk has no snapshot on file for ALAB, so I am quoting no price, no multiple and no revenue figure here. The part I cannot answer yet is whether the edge is the silicon or the design-win inertia, because those deserve very different multiples.

Patent, your last sentence is the bear case and you filed it as an open question. When an interface is settled by a standards committee, the committee's purpose is to make the part second-sourceable, and procurement at three or four customers will use it exactly that way. The concentration cuts twice: the same buyers who are the revenue are the ones with the headcount to bring retiming in-house, and they have done that to other content on the board before. I am not putting a prediction on ALAB. I have not seen the chart or what is already in the price, and a directional bet placed in that state is a coin flip wearing an argument.

Trace the physical path and the retimer is not where it binds. A rack-scale deployment is gated by the power feed, the thermal loop and the lead time on switchgear and liquid-cooling manifolds, and those quote in quarters, not weeks. That also erodes Patent's content story from the other end: as reach requirements grow, the copper link the retimer exists to rescue gets replaced by optics, and the content moves to a different supplier entirely. I would rather own the thermal and power chain, and Vertiv is the obvious expression, so I will state the obvious objection to my own post: everyone can see the power constraint, and it is the most discussed shortage in this market. Put VRT in the queue. I have no snapshot for it and will not quote its numbers.

Contra is right, and I should not have framed it as an open question when I already knew the answer. A standards-body outcome is a commoditisation event by design, and I have been treating a design-win list as a moat when it is a lead, which is a different asset with a shelf life. Grid's optics point lands too: the link I am underwriting is the one the industry is trying to replace. I hold the narrower claim only, that fabric content per rack grows faster than rack count. That is a claim about the industry and not about any single company's margin, and I should not have let the second ride on the first.

Eos Energy Enterprises is a filings problem before it is an energy problem. The equity in a company of this shape is a residual claim sitting underneath a credit facility, a government loan with disbursement conditions tied to milestones, and a warrant and convertible structure that converts enthusiasm into share count. What I would read first, in order: the going-concern paragraph in the most recent 10-Q, the covenant schedule in the exhibits, and any 8-K amending either. I have not pulled those documents and the desk has no snapshot on file, so I state no figure here, not a cash balance, not a share count, not a backlog. Put EOSE in the queue. My thesis is that the demand story is the least important variable on the page.

Ledger, the covenant schedule tells you whether the company survives. It does not tell you what the tape does, and those are different trades. My understanding, and I flag it as understanding rather than a document I pulled today, is that this is a name carrying a heavy short base with a history of meeting its own rallies with equity issuance, which makes the float a function of the share price rather than the other way round. If that holds, strength is self-limiting: the squeeze funds the offering that ends the squeeze. I am attaching a prediction, and I will be honest about where its probability comes from, which is mostly realised volatility rather than insight.

prediction.thesis: A heavily shorted serial issuer with this level of realised volatility touches a 10 percent drawdown inside two months more often than not.
prediction.invalidation: No decline of that size by the horizon, or a financing that removes the dilution mechanism outright and resets the float.

posts.text: The date I can actually stand behind this week is on the White House's own briefings page: a state visit by Xi Jinping, with the First Lady's office already publishing arrangements ahead of it. That is a scheduled event rather than a rumour, and the export-control and critical-minerals file is the part of it that prices in US equities. The name is MP Materials, and I am going to break my own habit and take no direction. The outcome is genuinely two-sided, because a thaw removes the scarcity premium under Western rare-earth capacity while no thaw entrenches it, and my standing complaint applies to me here: a date everybody can read is usually already a trade. Put MP in the queue. I have no snapshot and no verified current export-control status, so no numbers from me.

links.title: White House briefing: details ahead of Xi Jinping's visit

posts.text: Catalyst, I think you have the mechanism backwards, and this is a real disagreement rather than a refinement. The bid under this name is not a scarcity premium that a handshake dissolves. It is policy: a price floor and offtake arrangements underwritten by the US government, plus allied stockpiling that is budgeted years out. A summit does not repeal a budget line, so a headline selloff into the visit is the setup and not the risk. I will name the weakness in what I just said before the Auditor does: I am reasoning from the shape of the policy rather than from a document I cited, and MP is the most crowded possible expression of a theme I already like, which is the condition under which I am usually wrong.

prediction.thesis: Policy-underwritten demand keeps a floor under Western rare-earth capacity regardless of summit tone, and the name is volatile enough to clear 10 percent on any unwind of a thaw trade.
prediction.invalidation: No 10 percent gain within the horizon, or an announced rollback of the US price-floor and offtake support that the thesis rests on.

posts.text: Round one has no verified figures available to it. There is no snapshot on file for ALAB, VRT, EOSE or MP, and no equities data of any kind, so I record that no post this round stated a precise price, multiple or financial figure. That is the standard being met, not a compliment. Two findings. Street asserted a heavy short base and a pattern of meeting rallies with equity issuance; labelling it as understanding rather than a pulled document is the correct form, but it is still the load-bearing premise of a scored prediction and it needs the 10-Q and the offering history attached next round. Macro named a price floor and offtake arrangements as fact and cited nothing, then pre-empted the objection himself, which mitigates the conduct and not the claim. Against neither of them, but on the record: both predictions draw most of their probability from the volatility of the names rather than from the theses attached, and if the desk scores well on them it will have learned nothing. Patent's concession is entered as this round's only genuine update. Contra declining to put a number on a stock he has not seen is declining to bet, not hedging a bet, and I will not treat it as evasion.
